question: The ongoing project to upgrade the SS45 trunk road in Valtrebbia has met with strong opposition from the public and local authorities as a result both of the inconvenience caused and of the lack of any public consultation, a measure advocated in Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2836 of 12 December 2023 The project has also been modified since it was approved in 2017, and it is currently expected to cost EUR 230 million.

The current project includes as many as seven roundabouts along only 11 km and seriously diverges from the DNSH principle: countless tons of asphalt and concrete are to be laid for no reason, and the endless roadworks could bring businesses to their knees and have commuters tearing their hear out.

Upgrading the existing road, to supplement other renovation work already carried out, is not the problem; the issue is the nature of this project and its blithe disregard for the area and its inhabitants. This violation of the DNSH principle, the failure to listen to the public and the senselessly inflated project costs constitute a breach of EU rules.
Does the Commission not think it should request clarification from Italy on this project?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.6.2024) In the TEN-T (trans-European transport network) Regulation (EU) 1315/20131,2 the EU and the Member States have defined an EU-wide, multimodal network of rail, inland waterways, short sea shipping routes and roads which are linked to urban nodes, maritime and inland ports, airports and terminals which shall be jointly implemented to common standards and deadlines.

For infrastructures outside the TEN-T network, such as the SS45 trunk road, it is the sole responsibility of the respective Member States or of the project promoter to ensure compliance with legal requirements set in other legal acts such as the Environmental Impact Assessment Directive (which also introduces requirements for consultation of public)3.

Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2836 on promoting the engagement of citizens and civil society organisations in public policy-making processes encourages Member States to engage citizens and civil society organisations4 does not cover a specific policy area, it is up to the Member State concerned to decide whether to carry out a public consultation on multimodal transportation.

If a Member State decides to carry out such a consultation, the Recommendation, which is not legally binding, suggests a framework to do so. As regards the ‘do no significant harm’ (DNSH) principle/assessment this would only apply to the project if it were part of the recovery and resilience plan for Italy, which is not the case.

1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=uriserv:OJ.L_.2013.348.01.0001.01.ENG 2 Please note that a revised TEN-T regulation shall enter into force in June 2024 which however does not change

the status of the SS45 as a non-TEN-T road. 3 This project may fall under Annex II (point 10(e) and 13(a)) of the Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (OJ L 26, 28.1.2011), as amended by Directive 2014/52/EU (OJ L 124, 25.4.2014).

For projects covered by Annex II, Member States shall determine on a case-by-case examination or using pre-determined thresholds or criteria whether the project shall be made subject to an environmental impact assessment. 4 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32023H2836
